articles.title: 4 of Zaldy Co's ex-bodyguards issued arrest warrants; bail posted
articles.summary: Arrest warrants were issued against four out of 18 former bodyguards of ex-lawmaker Zaldy Co, but they were able to walk free after immediately posting bail.

blocks.text: Published September 11, 2026 5:25pm
Arrest warrants were issued against four out of 18 former bodyguards of ex-lawmaker Zaldy Co, but they were able to walk free after immediately posting bail.
In a DZBB report from Glen Juego on Friday, San Juan City police arrested four of the 18 ex-bodyguards due to a cyberlibel case filed against them.
San Juan City Chief of Police Col. Anthony Gantang confirmed the arrest directly to DZBB.
The arrest was made while the four ex-bodyguards were facing another case at the Hall of Justice in San Juan City.
Gantang said that the ex-bodyguards were able to walk free after posting bail on the same day at 4:00 p.m.
Each of them paid a bail of P10,000 for the cyberlibel complaint.

At least 10 other former bodyguards have been arrested due to perjury charges. The bodyguards, also known as maleta boys, made headlines for claiming to make cash deliveries for Co and several other personalities.
However, four out of the 18 have since recanted their testimonies, wanting to remain silent instead. —Jean Mangaluz/LDF, GMA News

articles.title: National Mourning Day for National Artist Resil Mojares on September 12
articles.summary: 'The nation will honor Mojares over his promotion of regional literature and history, as well as the formation of Cebuano and national identity,' Executive Secretary Ralph Recto says

blocks.text: REST IN PEACE. National Artist for Literature Resil B. Mojares dies at 83.
Leigh Go Mojares' Facebook
'The nation will honor Mojares over his promotion of regional literature and history, as well as the formation of Cebuano and national identity,' Executive Secretary Ralph Recto says
President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. has declared Saturday, September 12, as Day of National Mourning over the passing of National Artist for Literature Resil Mojares.

Under Proclamation No. 1434, signed by Executive Secretary Ralph Recto on behalf of the President, the nation will honor Mojares for his contributions as a “teacher, scholar, essayist, fictionist and historian, which contributed in the promotion of regional literature and history, as well as the formation of Cebuano and national identity.”

The proclamation said Mojares’ passing is a great loss to the Filipino people and the country’s cultural and artistic community. It also recognized his significant contribution to Philippine literature and cultural studies, which enriched the nation’s understanding and appreciation of its literary and cultural heritage.

As part of the national mourning, the Philippine flag shall be flown at half-mast from sunrise to sunset on September 12 at all government buildings and installations throughout the country. – Rappler.com

blocks.text: This is AI-generated. Read the article for full context. Report any errors.
The following is a press release from Maningning Miclat Art Foundation, Incorporated.
On the 26th anniversary of the death of trilingual poet, visual artist, teacher and translator Maningning Miclat, the Art Foundation named in her honor presents NINGNING SA DILIM.

The event features the awarding of winners of the 2026 Maningning Art Competition, the soft launch of Alma Cruz Miclat’s book Of Grief and Redemption (UP Press), an exhibit and sale of shortlisted competition entries, and a silent auction of paintings by Maningning from the Miclat family collection.
This will be held at the Art Circle Gallery in Bahay ng Alumni, UP Diliman on Saturday, September 19 at 4 pm.

From the shortlist of artists whose artworks will be on exhibit sale – Princess Ann Alegre, Jason Cedric Andres, Mica Collado, Marc Danpol Esurena, Ernest Uriel Malimban, Jealyn Samonte, Shari Eunice San Pablo, Maria Angelica Tejada, Maria Felicity Tejada, Julian Gabriel Cuison Trinidad and Jayrous Ehmard Vicent — will be chosen the Top 3.
The grand winner in the art competition will be awarded P28,000 cash prize and a Julie Lluch sculpture trophy.

The grand winner and the 2nd and 3rd prizes will receive copies of the Miclat books, including Maningning’s Voice from the Underworld, Fairground: A Literary Feast (Edited by Gémino H. Abad & Alma Cruz Miclat), Mario I. Miclat’s Memorial Set of his last three books – Kailan Diwata at 70+ na Tula, Hundred Flowers, Hundred Philosophies, and 21 West 4th Street, Ningning at Liwanag: Antolohiya ng 10 Nagwagi sa Gawad Maningning Miclat sa Tula [2003-2021], and coffee table book edition of Mario I. Miclat’s Secrets of the Eighteen Mansions with an Introduction by National Artist Virgilio S. Almario.
Selected paintings by Maningning Miclat will be on exhibit, most of which will be up for silent auction.
Meanwhile, the book, Of Grief and Redemption, will have a soft launching with the publisher UP Press getting pre-orders at launch price with delivery to be announced at a later date.

On Of Grief and Redemption, the author Alma Cruz Miclat’s rich story-telling in the last five years since the death of her beloved husband, poet, writer and academic Mario Ignacio Miclat, and her entry into the first half of the seventh decade of her life encapsulated in each of the 58 essays in the book, is a memoir on grief and loss, a journal on her struggle toward redemption.

Memories not only of those five years which she shared through different publications, but also of the half a century of living with the love of her life echo with grief and pain, especially since their multi-talented firstborn took her own life 26 years ago.

Multi-awarded publisher Karina Bolasco writes in the book’s Foreword: “The entire book is a purposive intimate meditation on love and loss, love as great as sunlight and loss as deep as six feet under. But there are roots that take root and bloom. It is about how on every ordinary day, Alma finds something, someone, somewhere with extraordinary stories to tell and share with others. She takes leaps of faith and whether or not she seeks it, there is somehow redemption, not only for her and her family and community but for a nation confronting daily its demons. For with the Miclats, and just by the manner of their past and present, we are certain there is nothing that is merely personal. Even grief and redemption.”

Thelma Sioson San Juan, Alma’s editor at TheDiarist.ph where the bulk of the essays came from, shares: “While others write to simply write, Alma Cruz Miclat writes to tell her own life story. In doing so, she bares her pain and tragedy, her happiness and triumph. Her own. Her honesty and bravery distinguish her writings. Her stories go beyond a display of craftsmanship; they bear witness to her own world and beyond it. She knows when to go deep into herself to share her longing for loved ones, and when to venture out to an outside world filled with injustice and untruths. She’s turned her memories—of sadness and joy—into a comfort zone, where even the reader is welcomed. Such is the generosity of this writer.”
For inquiries on the particulars of the event, email maningningfoundation@gmail.com. – Rappler.com

articles.title: Escudero will no longer vote on conviction rule --impeachment court spox
articles.summary: Senate impeachment court presiding officer Francis Escudero will no longer cast his vote on September 23, when senator-judges decide on whether or not to sustain the 16-vote threshold to convict Vice…

blocks.text: Senate impeachment court presiding officer Francis Escudero will no longer cast his vote on September 23, when senator-judges decide on whether or not to sustain the 16-vote threshold to convict Vice President Sara Duterte in her impeachment trial, court spokesperson Regie Tongol said Friday.

According to Tongol, Escudero stands by his ruling made when the impeachment trial began on July 6—that an affirmative vote by at least two-thirds of all 24 senators, or 16 votes, is needed for conviction.

“‘Yung kanyang ruling po, ‘yun na po ‘yung kanyang parang boto. At dahil ‘yung kanyang ruling ‘yung inaapela para i-kunsidera, of course, hindi niya na pwedeng i-withdraw ‘yun,” Tongol explained in a Zoom interview with Senate reporters.
(His ruling effectively serves as his vote. And since that ruling is the one being appealed for reconsideration, he can no longer withdraw his position.)
“Nakataga na ‘yun sa bato, ‘yung sa kanya. Kaya hindi na kinakailangan ‘yung kanyang boto on the floor,” he added.
(His position is set in stone. That’s why a vote from him on the floor is no longer necessary.)

If there will be 20 senator-judges present on September 23, including Escudero, the impeachment court spokesperson said that only 19 will vote. If that is the case, he noted that only a simple majority vote, or at least 10 affirmative votes, are needed to overturn the ruling.
“Majority of the quorum present po ang makakaboto po eh. Parang ordinary action lamang po ito ng Senado,” Tongol said.
(The votes of the majority of the quorum present will be the basis. This is just like an ordinary action of the Senate.)

Currently, Senators Jinggoy Estrada and Rodante Marcoleta are detained over separate plunder charges, while Senator Ronald “Bato” dela Rosa is in hiding amid an arrest warrant from the International Criminal Court.
Senator Loren Legarda, meanwhile, has not been attending the trial for weeks now as she is abroad on an extended medical leave.
Nevertheless, Tongol pointed out that there is still a possibility that the number of senator-judges who will be present on voting day will be higher than the expected 20.
Should there be a stalemate or equal votes coming from the senator-judges, he also said that it would mean that the motion pertaining to the voting threshold “failed.”

“So the ruling of the presiding officer will stand. Kasi po ang motion po is to appeal the ruling. So, kapag matalo po ‘yung boto on the floor, the ruling will stand. It is as if it is not changed and appealed,” he said.

(So the ruling of the presiding officer will stand. Because the motion was to appeal the ruling. So, if the vote on the floor does not get the majority, the ruling will stand. It is as if it is not changed and appealed.)

It was Senator-Judge Erwin Tulfo who made a manifestation during the impeachment trial on September 8, seeking clarification on the 16-voting threshold, given that four senator-judges are currently not attending the trial.
To settle the matter, Escudero said that the court will hear amici curiae (friends of the court) on September 16 to weigh in on the voting threshold.
The oral arguments between the defense and prosecution panels, meanwhile, will be held a week later or on September 23, with each side given 15 minutes to present its position.
After the oral arguments, senator-judges are also expected to cast their vote on the same day.
Amici Curiae
Meanwhile, Tongol cited the criteria that the presiding officer used in picking the legal experts who will provide views on the voting threshold.

“‘Yung credentials nila at saka ‘yung known expertise nila on the matter, pati ‘yung previous na mga experience nila in the framing of the Constitution. So kaya sila ‘yung mga napili at saka ‘yung kanilang known impartiality in their stance,” he explained.

(That was based on their credentials and their recognized expertise on the matter, as well as their prior experience in the framing of the Constitution. That’s why they were chosen—along with their known impartial stance.)

As of Thursday afternoon, the impeachment court said the participation of the following legal luminaries to physically appear before the court on September 16 to present their expert opinions has been “successfully secured:”
Retired Supreme Court Chief (SC) Justice Artemio PanganibanRetired SC Chief Justice Reynato PunoRetired SC Associate Justice Adolf Azcuna
Retired SC Chief Justice Hilario Davide will also be participating but only through a submission of a legal memorandum instead of physical appearance.
With this, the impeachment court expressed hope that the public would understand that all this is part of the democratic process.

“Sana maintindihan po ng publiko na parte po ito ng democratic processes natin para ‘yung gantong mga debate po ay lalo pong tumatalino lahat po ‘yung buong sambayanan, pati po ‘yung ating mga senator-judges at saka ‘yung parties,” Tongol said.

(I hope the public understands that this is part of our democratic processes. That through debates like this, everyone becomes better informed—the entire nation, as well as our senator-judges and the parties involved.)

“Kaya huwag po kayong mawalan ng tiwala na ‘yung ating mga senator-judge. Parang katulad ninyo rin po sila. Kung hanggang ngayon po may mga question diyan sa inyo, sa utak ninyo, ganun din po sila. May mga question din po sila at gusto nilang to finally put a nail in the coffin itong question na ito,” he added.

(So don’t lose faith in our senator-judges. They are just like you. If you have questions lingering in your minds, they do too. They also have questions and want to finally put this issue to rest.) —AOL, GMA News

articles.title: PH urges China to stop illegal activities in Mischief, Subi reefs
articles.summary: The Department of Foreign Affairs (DFA) on Friday called on China to halt its illegal occupation and activities in Panganiban Reef (Mischief Reef) and Zamora Reef (Subi Reef), maintaining that the…

blocks.text: Published September 11, 2026 5:09pm

The Department of Foreign Affairs (DFA) on Friday called on China to halt its illegal occupation and activities in Panganiban Reef (Mischief Reef) and Zamora Reef (Subi Reef), maintaining that the Philippines exercises sovereign rights and jurisdiction over these areas.

This came after the Philippine Coast Guard (PCG) said Chinese forces fired multiple flares at an unarmed PCG aircraft conducting a routine maritime domain awareness (MDA) flight over the Kalayaan Island Group (KIG) in the West Philippine Sea (WPS) on Monday.
According to the PCG, before landing on Pag-asa Island, the aircraft was challenged over the radio by Chinese forces illegally occupying Zamora (Subi) Reef, which then fired flares in its direction.
Chinese forces illegally occupying Panganiban (Mischief) Reef also reportedly repeated the same actions.

The DFA stressed that China’s island-building on both features violates Republic Act No. 12064 or the Philippine Maritime Zones Act, as well as the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea (UNCLOS), as confirmed by the 2016 arbitral award.
“We call on China to cease its illegal occupation and activities in Panganiban Reef and Zamora Reef immediately, and to abide by the final and binding 2016 Arbitral Award,” the DFA said.
The agency also said that China’s island-building “does not change the features’ legal status as a low-tide elevation.”

“As low-tide elevations, the Philippines exercises sovereign rights and jurisdiction over the features, and these can neither be the subject of a sovereignty claim nor capable of appropriation under international law,” the DFA added.

Following the incident, the DFA vowed to continue asserting the Philippines’ sovereignty, sovereign rights, and jurisdiction in the West Philippine Sea, and push for the country’s legitimate rights and interests in the maritime domain.—LDF, GMA News

articles.title: Oil, peso woes drag PSEi below 6,100
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — Local stocks fell below 6,100 on Friday as rising global oil prices and a weak peso stoked concerns about renewed inflationary pressures. The benchmark Philippine Stock Exchange…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — Local stocks fell below 6,100 on Friday as rising global oil prices and a weak peso stoked concerns about renewed inflationary pressures.
The benchmark Philippine Stock Exchange Index (PSEi) fell 0.61 percent, or 37.42 points, to close at 6,061.81.
Japhet Tantiangco, research manager at Philstocks Financial Inc., said inflation concerns weighed on market sentiment as Brent crude climbed past $100 per barrel.
The peso’s weakness added to investors’ worries, with both factors posing upside risks to consumer prices.
Higher global bond yields likewise dampened appetite for local equities, according to Tantiangco.
Luis Limlingan, head of sales at Regina Capital Development Corp., said elevated oil prices raised concerns about inflation and macroeconomic indicators, weighing on overall market sentiment.
“Meanwhile, the weaker local currency further encouraged investors to reduce risk exposure, keeping market pressure in place,” Limlingan said.
Trading remained tepid, with net value turnover reaching P5.83 billion.
Subdued market activity

Foreign investors also continued to pull funds out of the local market, ending the session as net sellers with net outflows of P999.47 million. Nearly all sectoral indices finished negative. The property sector was the lone exception, closing flat.
Mining and oil suffered the steepest decline, shedding 3.27 percent.
Among index members, Century Pacific Food Inc. bucked the broader market downturn. The stock jumped 5.31 percent to P33.70, making it Friday’s top PSEi performer.
Meanwhile, GT Capital Holdings Inc. led the laggards. Shares of the conglomerate dropped 3.44 percent to P448.80.
Analysts said the market’s decline reflected growing caution over the inflation outlook as expensive oil and a weaker local currency threaten to raise costs.
Persistent foreign selling and rising global bond yields added pressure, while subdued trading indicated that investors remained cautious amid uncertainties at home and abroad. /pai

articles.summary: The Sandiganbayan Sixth Division grants the motions for reconsideration of former police generals Tomas Rentoy III and Gil Meneses and Colonel Regino Catiis, setting aside their graft conviction in…

blocks.text: ANTI-GRAFT COURT. The Sandiganbayan in Quezon City.
Jansen Romero/Rappler

The Sandiganbayan Sixth Division grants the motions for reconsideration of former police generals Tomas Rentoy III and Gil Meneses and Colonel Regino Catiis, setting aside their graft conviction in December 2025

items: The Sandiganbayan acquitted former police generals Tomas Rentoy III and Gil Meneses, and Colonel Regino Catiis of graft related to the illegal issuance of rifle licenses.
The court found that the prosecution failed to provide credible evidence regarding the authenticity of the Authority to Purchase Firearms documents and the signatures involved.
While some officials were acquitted, the court upheld the convictions of other police personnel and a businessman for their roles in the illegal firearms licensing scheme.

blocks.text: This is AI-generated. Read the article for full context. Report any errors.
MANILA, Philippines – The anti-graft court Sandiganbayan has acquitted two former police generals and a police colonel of graft in connection to the illegal issuance of rifle licenses.

The Sandiganbayan Sixth Division granted the motions for reconsideration filed by former police generals Tomas Rentoy III and Gil Meneses and Colonel Regino Catiis, setting aside their graft conviction in December 2025.

The cases involved the alleged anomalous processing, approval, and release of hundreds of high-power firearms to a private security agency in 2011 and 2012, in violation of the Anti-Graft and Corrupt Practices Act or Republic Act No. 3019.
In granting Rentoy’s motion for reconsideration, the court noted that his previous conviction was based on three memoranda bearing the subject “Authority to Purchase Firearms.”

“After a careful re-evaluation of the evidence, the Court finds that the prosecution failed to establish, by competent and credible proof, the existence, authenticity, and official provenance of the alleged original Authority to Purchase Firearms (ATPFs),” the court said.

As for Catiis, the court cited the testimony of handwriting expert witness Edwardo del Rosario that Catiis’ supposed signature on the Applications for Firearms License (AFLs) and his genuine signature “were not written by one and the same person.”

“Notably, the specimen signatures utilized as standards were taken from documents bearing accused Catiis’ signatures, which form part of the official records of the PNP, thereby lending additional credence to the reliability of the examination,” the Sixth Division said.

In the case of Meneses, the court said: “This fact stands unrefuted. In view of his lack of authority to license, approve, or recommend approval, accused Meneses could not have exercised discretion in the issuance of ATPFs.”

On December 5, 2025, the anti-graft court found the following PNP officials and personnel guilty beyond reasonable of multiple counts of graft: former police generals Raul Petrasanta, Rentoy, Gil Meneses, and Napoleon Estilles; colonels Eduardo Acierto, Allan Parreño, and Regino Catiis; Major Nelson Bautista; Master Sergeant Randy de Sesto; non-uniformed personnel Sol Bargan; and businessman Isidro Lozada, owner of Caraga Security Agency.
In its latest ruling the court affirmed the conviction of Estilles, Bautista, Zapata, De Sesto, and Lozada.

“Verily, in the performance of their official functions, accused Bautista, Zapata, and De Sesto cannot now disclaim responsibility by asserting lack of authority to evaluate the regularity of the firearms license applications. Public accountability attaches not to formal titles alone, but to the actual discharge of official functions,” the court said.
The explanations of the rest of the accused failed to convince the court that they had no participation in the conferment of unwarranted benefit to Lozada and the Caraga Security Agency.

Based on case records, prosecutors traced hundreds of AK-47 and CZ858 rifles purchased by the Caraga Security Agency supposedly for the JTC Mineral Mining Corporation, Isla Security Agency, and Claver Mineral Development Corporation.
Several of the imported firearms, however, were later recovered after encounters with the New People’s Army in Agusan del Sur in 2013. – Rappler.com

Merkel: 'There is no free lunch' for democracy

blocks.caption: Merkel has rarely made public appearances since leaving office in 2021Image: Jens Krick/Flashpic/picture alliance

blocks.text: Former German Chancellor Angela Merkel has urged people to actively defend democracy and freedom, warning that democratic principles cannot be taken for granted.
"There's no free lunch — nothing comes for free," Merkel told around 1,200 people at a reading from her memoir "Freedom" in Peenemünde on the Baltic Sea island of Usedom.
"You are getting a small assignment too," the former leader of the center-right Christian Democratic Union (CDU) told the audience.
Merkel read from a passage in her book in which she argues that truth and lies are increasingly being deliberately blurred, including by people in positions of power in democratic countries.
"Freedom needs democratic conditions. Without democracy, there is no freedom," Merkel said.
She urged people to defend democratic institutions against those who threaten them.
"If we want to live in freedom, we have to defend our democracy against those who threaten it," Merkel said.
She added that this could succeed "if we work together, if we get involved together, each of us individually and all of us for one another."

Merkel acknowledged that some of the decisions made during her time in office had contributed to support for the far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD), including her response to the 2015 refugee crisis and her policies during the eurozone debt crisis.

articles.title: ‘Kumong Bol-Anon 26’: Suganob, Nontshinga promise wins on eve of rematch
articles.summary: All roads lead to “Kumong Bol-Anon 26” as Boholano Regie “Filipino Phenom” Suganob gets another shot at redemption against his former tormentor, two-time world champion Sivenathi “The Chosen One”…

blocks.text: TAGBILARAN CITY, Philippines — All roads lead to “Kumong Bol-Anon 26” as Boholano Regie “Filipino Phenom” Suganob gets another shot at redemption against his former tormentor, two-time world champion Sivenathi “The Chosen One” Nontshinga, in the main event on Saturday, Sept. 12, at the Bohol Wisdom School here.

Three years after their first encounter in South Africa in 2023, Suganob and Nontshinga are set to settle their unfinished business in a high-stakes 12-round International Boxing Federation (IBF) light flyweight world title eliminator.
Nontshinga won their first meeting by unanimous decision in 2023 to retain his IBF world title, handing the then-inexperienced Suganob his first professional defeat.
A lot has changed since then.

Suganob has won all five of his fights since the loss and has climbed to No. 1 in both the IBF and World Boxing Organization (WBO) light flyweight rankings. He has also captured the WBO Global title and successfully defended it several times, beating a number of world-ranked opponents along the way.
Nontshinga seeks comeback

Nontshinga, meanwhile, has gone 2-2 in his last four fights and has since been stripped of his IBF world championship after losing it to Masamichi Yabuki in Japan in 2024, the same year he reclaimed it from Adrian Curiel via a rematch held in Mexico.
With everything on the line, both fighters vowed to leave no doubt when they meet again.
At Friday’s official weigh-in in Panglao, Suganob came in at 107.9 pounds, while Nontshinga weighed 107.5 pounds, with both fighters comfortably making the 108-pound limit for their title eliminator.
IBF president Daryl Peoples supervised the weigh-in, while renowned international referee Tony Weeks is set to serve as the third man in the ring.
Suganob, who has grown considerably since their first encounter, believes he is a completely different fighter this time around.

“Daghan na ug kalahian ang sauna ug karon. Mas ni-matured nako karon, mas daghan nako ug nakat-unan, ug mas confident ko karon nga modaog. Mao nang kumpyansa ko modaug ani nga fight by knockout,” said Suganob.
His promoter and manager, PMI Bohol Boxing Promotions head Floriezyl Echavez Podot, shares the same confidence.

“Makita namo nga mas ni-improve si Regie sukad atong pagkapildi niya ni Nontshinga atong 2023. Karon mas kusog, mas matured ug mas confident si Regie, mao nang dako ko ug kumpyansa nga iyaha nang ma-knockout si Nontshinga karon nga fight,” said Podot.
Unfazed opponent
Nontshinga, however, remains unfazed by Suganob’s renewed confidence.
The South African already knows what it takes to beat Suganob, having dropped him once and outpointed him in their first meeting.
Asked about his edge over Suganob aside from their first fight, Nontshinga pointed to his talent, conditioning and strategy.
“Everything that I have, things that I learned at home and the team and the people I worked with. Those are the advantages I have,” said Nontshinga.
“I’ll always be the better fighter. I’m the better boxer. I will showcase that to the whole world.”
Despite the verbal exchanges, both fighters maintained respect for each other during the final faceoff, creating a different kind of tension ahead of what promises to be an explosive rematch.
Three other IBF regional titles will also be contested on the card.
Cebuano prospect Reymart Tagacanao of Carcar City, who fights out of Villamor Boxing Gym and PMI Bohol Boxing Promotions, will battle China’s Chunlin Kuang for the IBF Asia junior bantamweight title.
PMI fighter Leonard Pores III will face Indonesia’s Andika Fredrikson Hae for the IBF Pan Pacific flyweight title.
In the opening bout, Datu Adam will take on another Indonesian, Oky Akbar, for the IBF Asia junior featherweight championship.
The first bout is scheduled for 6 p.m.

articles.title: Philippines tells China to end 'illegal occupation' of Panganiban, Zamora reefs
articles.summary: DFA says reclamation cannot change the reefs' legal status.

blocks.text: September 11, 2026 | 4:56pm
This satellite image retrieved February 18, 2021 shows China's structures on Mischief or Panganiban Reef in the South China Sea.
Google Maps / Maxar Technologies

MANILA, Philippines — The Department of Foreign Affairs reaffirmed the Philippines' sovereign rights and jurisdiction over Panganiban (Mischief) Reef and Zamora (Subi) Reef in the West Philippine Sea, and called on China to "cease its illegal occupation and activities" on both features.
In a statement on Friday, September 11, the DFA said the two reefs are low-tide elevations within the Philippines' exclusive economic zone (EEZ) and continental shelf.
A low-tide elevation is a naturally formed feature that is above water at low tide but submerged at high tide.
Because of this status, the DFA said, the reefs "can neither be the subject of a sovereignty claim nor capable of appropriation under international law."

The department said China's island-building on both reefs violates UNCLOS and Republic Act 12064 or the Philippine Maritime Zones Act, and "does not change the features' legal status as a low-tide elevation."
It also urged Beijing to abide by the 2016 arbitral award, which is "final and binding."
Flare incident

The statement came a day after the Philippine Coast Guard confirmed that Chinese forces fired flares toward an unarmed PCG aircraft conducting a maritime domain awareness flight over the Kalayaan Island Group on Monday, September 7.
Chinese forces on Zamora Reef challenged the aircraft over radio and then fired flares in its direction before the plane landed on Pag-asa Island, according to the PCG.
Chinese forces on Panganiban Reef did the same, the PCG said.

PCG Commandant Adm. Ronnie Gil Gavan said firing flares at an aircraft in flight endangers flight safety and disregards China's duty of due regard under the Convention on International Civil Aviation.
The PCG said they also observed a considerable number of Chinese maritime militia vessels sheltered inside the lagoons of both reefs.
China has built artificial islands on both reefs, which lie in the Spratly Islands west of Palawan.

The 2016 ruling, issued by an arbitral tribunal in a case filed by the Philippines under UNCLOS, found that China's sweeping "nine-dash line" claim over most of the South China Sea has no legal basis.
It also classified Panganiban Reef as a low-tide elevation forming part of the Philippines' EEZ and continental shelf.

articles.title: 9/11 attacks: Trial remains elusive for purported mastermind
articles.summary: Two decades after U.S. authorities locked Khalid Sheikh Mohammed away at a military detention center in Cuba, the purported mastermind of the Sept. 11 attacks sometimes seems barely any closer to…

blocks.text: NEW YORK — Two decades after U.S. authorities locked Khalid Sheikh Mohammed away at a military detention center in Cuba, the purported mastermind of the September 11 attacks sometimes seems barely any closer to being put on trial than the day he arrived.

A judge recently set a 2028 date for Mohammed to finally be tried before a military tribunal, but some lawyers predict it will never happen — not that year or any other year. They say the maze of legal issues that arose because Mohammed was tortured following his 2003 capture in Pakistan is too twisted to ever be straightened out.
A fleeting bid to put him on trial in a civilian court in New York City was shouted down years ago over security concerns.

A plea agreement that would have kept Mohammed imprisoned for life, but spared him from a possible execution, began to collapse shortly after it was announced in 2024, and finally died for good last year.
“It’s all contaminated by politics and the lack of accountability on torture,” said Joshua Dratel, an attorney who played a part in assuring that Mohammed has proper legal representation.

In late August, the U.S. military judge who set a June 5, 2028, trial date for Mohammed and three others charged in the Sept. 11 attacks ruled that prosecutors could not use an alleged confession he made to the FBI in 2007. Those statements were deemed tainted because Mohammed was subjected to “enhanced interrogation techniques” overseas, including the simulated drowning technique called waterboarding.
Blow to the prosecution
While the ruling was a blow to the prosecution, the U.S. government decided not to appeal, in part because doing so could have further delayed a possible trial.
Meanwhile, Mohammed remains jailed in Guantanamo Bay, where he was brought on Sept. 5, 2006, following more than three years in secret prisons in other countries.
Victims’ families still hope a trial will happen
Terry Strada, whose husband, Tom, died at the World Trade Center on Sept. 11, said that she and other people who lost family members still hope a trial will someday happen.
“We very much want to see this come to an end at some point. We do want to see justice served. It’s just as important as 25 years ago,” she said.

But Strada, the national chair of the group 9/11 Families United, also said she would rather have Mohammed rot at Guantanamo Bay indefinitely than get behind a resolution that would involve dropping the death penalty as a possibility. Strada said she worries that if Mohammed is not executed, future U.S. leaders might someday be tempted to swap him for Americans held prisoner elsewhere in the world.
The death penalty, she said, “fits the crime and it would prevent that from ever happening. And that’s important to me.”

Mohammed was captured in Pakistan in 2003, accused of developing and directing the 9/11 attacks, as a leader of the Islamic militant group al-Qaida. Some of the delays in his legal proceedings have stemmed from his treatment after he fell into U.S. control. A U.S. Senate report pointed to his extended torture in CIA custody, including 183 sessions of waterboarding.
Plans for a civilian trial were dropped

For a time in 2009, it seemed Mohammed was headed to New York after then-Attorney General Eric Holder announced plans to try him and four other men charged in the Sept. attacks in a Manhattan courthouse just blocks from the World Trade Center site.
Then-President Barack Obama, who had pledged to close the Guantanamo detention center, said Mohammed would face “the most exacting demands of justice.”

Almost immediately, opposition arose. Some critics predicted Mohammed would use a trial as a platform to spread hateful views of America and its allies. Others cited security concerns, saying it could again make New York a terrorist target. Former New York City Mayor Rudy Giuliani, a Republican, called the plan unwise and said it showed “a lack of concern for the rights of the public.”
Plans for a civilian trial were dropped.
“It was a charade in many respects,” Dratel said.
The military tribunal system, he said, has proven itself to be a worse solution, unable to function efficiently, without a proper structure and without fidelity to federal courts.
“Each time you reach an impasse, no one knows what to do,” he said.

David Raskin, a Washington lawyer now in private practice who would have led the government’s prosecution of Mohammed in New York if it hadn’t been abandoned, said in an essay published in The Washington Post on Wednesday that he is confident a civilian trial would have ended with a conviction. The military commissions, on the other hand, “became a defense lawyer’s dream,” beset by “endless litigation over their legality and procedures.”
“I predict there will never be a completed military commission trial for Mohammed and the other Sept. 11 defendants,” he said.

articles.title: Hong Kong Tiananmen activists sentenced up to 7 years
articles.summary: Three pro-democracy activists who organized annual commemorations of China's deadly 1989 Tiananmen crackdown were charged under Hong Kong's Beijing-backed national security law.

image.caption: Vigils commemorating Tiananmen massacre are essentially outlawed under Hong Kong's security laws [FILE JUNE 2021]Image: Kin Cheung/AP Photo/picture alliance

blocks.text: A Hong Kong court on Friday sentenced three pro-democracy activists who organized annual vigils marking China's deadly 1989 Tiananmen crackdown to between five and seven years in prison under the city's national security law.
The sentences handed down were:

items: Lee Cheuk-yan, 69 — seven years
Chow Hang-tung, 41 — seven years and three months.
Albert Ho, 74, — five years and two months, after pleading guilty

blocks.text: The three were convicted in August of "incitement to subversion" over their activities with the now-disbanded Hong Kong Alliance, which received a fine of HK$1.5 million ($191,304, €164,768). The alliance had organized annual Tiananmen vigils in Victoria Park.
Defendants deny charges
Judges cited the group's call to "end one-party dictatorship," saying it challenged the legitimacy of Communist Party rule in the Chinese special administrative region.

blocks.caption: Lee Cheuk-yan, Chow Hang-tung and Albert Ho were charged under Hong Kong's controversial national security lawImage: Peter Parks/Anthony Wallace/AFP

blocks.text: Lee and Chow denied the subversion charges under Hong Kong's controversial national security law. The defendants also insisted the alliance had not asked people to do anything illegal.

The court rejected arguments that the defendants believed they were acting within the law given Hong ​Kong's freedoms of speech, which have been severely curtailed since Beijing imposed the law in 2020 following a crackdown mass pro-democracy protests the previous year.
The vigils, once a major annual event in Hong Kong, have been effectively banned under the law.
Chow, a barrister who represented herself, raised both arms and waved at supporters as she was escorted out.
Her mother, Medina Chow, addressed her supporters saying, "For today's verdict, you do not need to be overly saddened. Do not lose heart. And above all, do not ​feel guilty."

blocks.caption: Chow told a hearing last month that she had 'nothing to repent for' [FILE: June 5, 2021]Image: Kin Cheung/AP Photo/picture alliance

blocks.text: What is the international reaction?
The convictions have drawn criticism from foreign governments and rights groups.

"This sentencing is a triple tragedy: for the activists being unjustly punished; the survivors and victims of the Tiananmen crackdown itself; and the generations of Hongkongers denied the space to discuss one of the most consequential events in modern Chinese history," said Amnesty International's deputy regional director, Sarah Brooks.
Germany and France last month had condemned the verdict against Chow saying that "peaceful advocacy for human rights does not constitute a crime."
Chow was the recipient of Franco-German Human Rights Award in 2023.
Among those arrested under the security law are pro-democracy former media tycoon Jimmy Lai and former student leader Joshua Wong.

articles.title: Toledo father arrested after allegedly shooting son during argument
articles.summary: CEBU CITY, Philippines — A 60-year-old man was arrested on Thursday afternoon, September 10, after allegedly shooting his son with a handgun in Purok 7, Barangay Daanlungsod, Toledo City, Cebu.…

blocks.text: CEBU CITY, Philippines — A 60-year-old man was arrested on Thursday afternoon, September 10, after allegedly shooting his son with a handgun in Purok 7, Barangay Daanlungsod, Toledo City, Cebu.
Authorities identified the suspect as alias “Sunny,” 60, married, and a resident of the area. The victim was identified as his 30-year-old son, alias “Mark.”
According to the Toledo City Police Station, the victim personally reported the incident to police at around 4:00 p.m.
He alleged that they were having an argument until it turned into an altercation, with his father pulling out a gun and firing at him.
The victim managed to escape unharmed by taking cover behind a concrete wall after the initial shot missed.
He immediately fled the scene and ran directly to the police station for help.
Responding officers, led by Police Senior Master Sergeant Mark Anthony Salvacion, arrived at the scene around 4:30 p.m.
Upon arrival, police recovered one spent .45 caliber cartridge case from the ground and spotted the suspect outside his house.
Police negotiators successfully convinced the suspect to surrender peacefully.
He turned over a .45 caliber pistol loaded with one live round in the chamber, an empty magazine, and a black inside-the-waistband holster.
When law enforcement asked for his License to Own and Possess Firearms (LTOPF), or legal authorization permit for the weapon, the suspect failed to present any valid documentation.
The suspect was placed under arrest, informed of his constitutional rights, and taken to the Toledo City Police Station for booking and custodial investigation.

Under the supervision of Toledo Police Chief Police Lieutenant Colonel Verniño B. Noserale, police are preparing criminal charges against the suspect for Attempted Parricide under the Revised Penal Code and Illegal Possession of Firearms and Ammunition (Republic Act No. 10591) before the Prosecutor’s Office.

articles.title: FACT CHECK: Photos of Sara Duterte visiting MILF camp ahead of 2026 polls are fake
articles.summary: ‘Based on what we have, she did not visit the region recently,’ the Police Regional Office Bangsamoro Autonomous Region told Rappler in a text message

blocks.text: Claim: Vice President Sara Duterte visited a camp of the Moro Islamic Liberation Front (MILF) and was warmly received by Bangsamoro Islamic Armed Forces (BIAF) fighters.

Why we fact-checked this: The claim began spreading on Facebook as early as September 8, using supposed photos of the Vice President surrounded by alleged BIAF fighters. The photos are also circulating on TikTok, Reddit, YouTube, and Instagram.
The most popular post came from a page using the Bangsamoro Islamic Armed Forces name. It drew roughly 4,000 comments and 5,000 shares.

Its caption read: “Sa pagkakaalam ko, mas mataas ang respeto ng mga MILF kay VP Sara kaysa sa AFP (Armed Forces of the Philippines) at PNP (Philippine National Police)… hindi raw siya safe sa lahat ng mga nakapaligid sa kanya.”
(As far as I know, the MILF has more respect for VP Sara than the AFP and PNP… she’s reportedly not safe around everyone surrounding her.)
There are multiple versions of the claim using the same photos. Some of them placed the alleged visit at Camp Darapanan, MILF’s main base in Sultan Kudarat, Maguindanao del Norte.

The facts: The Police Regional Office Bangsamoro Autonomous Region told Rappler in a text message on Friday, September 11, that they received no coordination or information about any recent visit of Duterte to the Bangsomoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao (BARMM).
“Based on what we have, she did not visit the region recently,” they said.

There is also no public record of the supposed visit on the Office of the Vice President (OVP)’s official Facebook page, its regional OVP satellite offices, Duterte’s own Facebook account, the Bangsamoro Government’s official Facebook page, or Luwaran, the MILF Central Committee’s official information website.
The Bangsamoro Government has separately warned the public about fake pages impersonating official Bangsamoro channels.
Camp Darapanan, where the visit supposedly happened, is also the site of former president Rodrigo Duterte’s real, documented 2016 visit with MILF leaders, also reported on Luwaran.

AI-generated photos, suspicious pages: Artificial intelligence detection tools Hive Moderation and Image Whisperer flagged both photos as likely to be AI-generated (84% and 91%, and high spatial frequency variance in the tactical gear and crowd, respectively).

Reverse image searches found no exact match for either of the two viral photos. However, the closest visual match found is from Duterte’s June 2026 visit to Nunungan, Lanao del Norte, for the 60th Araw ng Nunungan celebration.
A frame from video coverage of the same visit, at the 0:33 mark, closely resembles the framing used in the modified viral photo, suggesting the fake images were likely edited from this real footage.
Pages spreading the claim — such as the one using the Bangsamoro Islamic Armed Forces name — were created on September 5, just four days before the claim began circulating.

Securing the elections: This claim surfaced in the final days of campaigning for the first-ever BARMM parliamentary elections to be held on Monday, September 14. The event marks a historic milestone in the region’s transition from the 2014 peace agreement between the Philippine government and the MILF to a functioning parliamentary system. (LIVE UPDATES: First BARMM parliamentary elections)
Debunked: Rappler has previously debunked other false claims involving BARMM officials and the upcoming elections:

items: FACT CHECK: News of 39 soldiers held by MILF is from 2023, not recent
FACT CHECK: No Turkish police deployed to secure BARMM polls
FACT CHECK: No reports of MNLF, MILF plot vs Marcos gov’t over Duterte arrest
FACT CHECK: BARMM official’s ‘hate quote’ after MSU bombing is fake

blocks.text: – James Bones/Rappler.com
James Bones is a Research and Data volunteer at Rappler. He is a fourth-year Bachelor of Science in Industrial Engineering student at the Polytechnic University of the Philippines – Manila.

Keep us aware of suspicious Facebook pages, groups, accounts, websites, articles, or photos in your network by contacting us at factcheck@rappler.com. Let us battle disinformation one Fact Check at a time.

articles.title: Philippines tells China: Leave Panganiban, Zamora reefs in West PH Sea
articles.summary: China fired flares at an unarmed Philippine Coast Guard aircraft as it flew near Panganiban Reef and Zamora Reef en route to Pag-asa Island last September 7

blocks.text: SUBI REEF. Video from the Philippine Coast Guard shows flares being fired from Subi Reef on September 7, 2026.
Philippine Coast Guard
China fired flares at an unarmed Philippine Coast Guard aircraft as it flew near Panganiban Reef and Zamora Reef en route to Pag-asa Island last September 7

items: The Philippine Department of Foreign Affairs (DFA) urged China to cease its militarization and illegal activities in Panganiban Reef and Zamora Reef, asserting the Philippines' sovereign rights over these areas.
Chinese forces recently fired flares at a Philippine Coast Guard aircraft near these reefs, which are part of the Philippines' exclusive economic zone in the South China Sea.

The DFA emphasized that China's actions violate international law, specifically the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea (UNCLOS) and a 2016 Arbitral Award that supports the Philippines' claims.

blocks.text: This is AI-generated. Read the article for full context. Report any errors.

MANILA, Philippines — The Department of Foreign Affairs (DFA) reiterated on Friday, September 11, Manila’s call for Beijing to leave militarized reefs in the West Philippine Sea, days after China fired flares at a Philippine Coast Guard (PCG) aircraft.
“We call on China to cease its illegal occupation and activities in Panganiban Reef and Zamora Reef immediately, and to abide by the final and binding 2016 Arbitral Award,” said the DFA.

On September 7, Chinese forces in Panganiban Reef (Mischief Reef) and Zamora Reef (Subi Reef) fired flares at an unarmed PCG aircraft as it was en route to Pag-asa Island. All these features are part of the West Philippine Sea, a body of water that includes the Philippines’ exclusive economic zone (EEZ) in the South China Sea.

blocks.caption: Philippines tells China: Leave Panganiban, Zamora reefs in West PH Sea

blocks.text: Chinese embassy in Manila deputy spokesperson Guo Wei, in a statement, earlier insisted in a statement that China had “jurisdiction” over the two reefs, which they consider to the part of the Nansha Islands, which they claim as their territory.
Both reefs are low-tide elevations where sovereignty cannot be claimed, based on the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea (UNCLOS), which China is signatory to.
In a statement, the DFA said that since the reefs are within the Philippines’ EEZ and continental shelf, it’s Manila that has “sovereign rights and jurisdiction over the features.”

The DFA added: “China’s island-building on both features violates the Philippine Maritime Zones Act (Republic Act 12064) and UNCLOS, as confirmed by the Award, and does not change the features’ legal status as a low-tide elevation.”

China claims almost all of the South China Sea, including the West Philippine Sea, as its territory — a stand that’s contradictory to UNCLOS. Beijing also rejects the 2016 Arbitral Award, a landmark ruling based on UNCLOS, that affirmed the entitlements and rights of the Philippines based on the same convention.

Bilateral ties between the two countries have been especially tense in recent years, primarily over disputes in the West Philippine Sea and China’s incursions. Those tensions have also spilled beyond the maritime space. Last year, China imposed sanctions on former senator Francis Tolentino, who is now labor chief, and sanctioned Defense Secretary Gilberto Teodoro Jr. just in 2026. – Rappler.com

articles.title: Why do we always root for the anti-heroes?
articles.summary: They lie, cheat, manipulate and betray. They make one questionable decision after another, cross moral lines and sometimes even commit a crime or two. They are the embodiment of the term “red flag,”…

blocks.text: They lie, cheat, manipulate and betray. They make one questionable decision after another, cross moral lines and sometimes even commit a crime or two. They are the embodiment of the term “red flag,” with barely a redeeming quality in sight–yet somehow, they still manage to captivate fans.

There is a strange loyalty that comes with having a favorite anti-hero. The kind that makes fans overlook their worst decisions, defend their most questionable actions, and, at times, argue that they aren’t as bad as everyone else views them to be.
Yes, they are flawed, but after spending hours watching their stories unfold, it becomes difficult to simply write them off as villains.
“A girl will choose her favorite anti-hero and stick with it”
But what exactly makes someone anti-hero?
Merriam-Webster defines the term as “a protagonist or notable figure who is conspicuously lacking in heroic qualities.”

Unlike the traditional heroes, an anti-hero does not always have a moral compass, selflessness or nobility that are usually associated with protagonists such as Superman or Spider-Man. They can be selfish, violent, manipulative, or driven by their personal motives that are far from heroic.

Author Stephanie Brown similarly defined an anti-hero as “a main character that we root for despite their obvious flaws, bad behavior, or seeming immorality.” Their actions, she added, drive the narrative as they pursue a goal that doesn’t necessarily have to be noble.

Ellie from the video game ‘The Last of Us Part II’ is a prime example. After Abby Anderson kills Joel in retaliation for her father’s death, Ellie sets out on a path of revenge that gradually blurs the line between protagonist and antagonist.

Driven by grief and anger, she leaves a trail of violence in her pursuit of Abby, pushing her further from the character players once knew. Yet her pain, past, and vulnerability make it difficult to simply turn against her.
V from ‘V for Vendetta’ is another compelling example. His methods are difficult to defend, but his cause helps audiences understand and even support him.

Behind the mask, V uses violence, deception, and destruction to fight an oppressive government. His actions may be morally questionable, but his fight for justice and freedom gives viewers a reason to root for him anyway.
They’re not exactly heroes, but they aren’t always written as straightforward villains either. Instead, they exist somewhere in the messy middle—where audiences seem to love meeting them.
And maybe that messy middle is exactly where the thrill begins. There’s something inherently compelling about characters whose actions we condemn, yet whose fate we still care about.

As it turns out, our fascination with morally questionable characters isn’t entirely irrational. Research on anti-heroes found that audience identification plays a role in how much viewers like morally questionable characters.

“One explanation for identification’s role in the enjoyment of antiheroes may be that viewers perceive such characters as more realistic than their near-perfect traditional hero counterparts,” researchers Sophia Janicke and Arthur Raney stated.
Unlike traditional heroes who often embody clear-cut ideals of courage and morality, anti-heroes are defined by their flaws, contradictions, and imperfect choices.
And fans themselves seem to understand the appeal. In a Reddit discussion on anti-heroes, commenters pointed to the appeal of characters who are far from the traditional “good guy.”

blocks.caption: Anti-hero characters
Anti-hero characters

blocks.text: One Redditor said that it’s easier to connect with characters who “share our foibles and problems” than with heroes who represent an almost impossible ideal. Another commenter put it more simply: anti-heroes “start from desires and needs that we understand.”
Fiction gives audiences something real life rarely does: a front-row seat to someone’s thoughts.
We see their past, insecurities, relationships and motivations. We witness what happened before they made the wrong decision, and sometimes, we even understand why they thought it was the right one.
That context can make a character easier to sympathize with. It doesn’t necessarily make their actions right. It simply makes them human—and perhaps makes it easier to see ourselves in them.

When we think about it, we may not relate to committing a crime or betraying someone, but we can understand wanting to be loved, feeling rejected, being angry at the world, or making a decision out of fear. Anti-heroes take those very human emotions and push them to extremes.
“Mama, I’m in love with a criminal”
Sometimes, it’s not just the character but how the story tells us to see them. The more time we spend with their fears and struggles, the harder it becomes to simply label them as “the bad guy.”
We may not agree with their choices, but understanding where they come from can make us hesitate before completely giving up on them.

Once known as the Winter Soldier, Bucky Barnes spent years being used as a weapon and forced to commit violent acts against his will. While the damage he caused can’t simply be undone, seeing his struggle to reclaim his identity and make peace with his past gives audiences someone to sympathize with.
Even ‘Loki’ head writer Michael Waldron believes that Bucky is the best character from the Marvel Cinematic Universe to receive the same treatment as the God of Mischief.

“I love Bucky. I think Bucky is a great character. Like Loki, that’s somebody who has a lot of trauma that they’re working through, but there’s a real vulnerability and likeability there. So, I like Bucky a lot,” Waldron said.

And perhaps that is what makes Bucky’s appeal lie. Characters like Bucky are the kind of characters audiences want to see win. Audiences don’t root for him because his past has been disregarded, nor are his actions simply erased, but because they’ve witnessed his struggle to move beyond it.
There is something deeply satisfying about watching him, who was once defined by what was done to him, reclaim the agency to decide who he wants to become.

Loki, on the other hand, follows a different path. He was a selfish, manipulative god who was constantly caught between wanting power and wanting to belong. Yet as audiences got to see more of his loneliness, insecurities and complicated relationship with his family and himself, the villain becomes someone much easier to understand.

His redemption feels rewarding precisely because we’ve seen how difficult it is for him to get there. It has been shown to us time and time again how awful and deceitful he could be, but what kept us watching was the possibility that he could choose differently.

And when a character finally breaks from the patterns after a history of poor choices, it becomes difficult not to hope or root for their redemption. The ending of ‘Loki’ Season 2 proved this, as Loki ultimately sacrificed himself to hold the timelines together, choosing others’ freedom over his own.
But not every morally gray character follows the same path.
Walter White from ‘Breaking Bad’ is perhaps one of the clearest examples of how storytelling can keep audiences engaged with a character even as his actions become increasingly difficult to defend.
The story begins with a struggling teacher who wants to provide for his family and watch as that motivation slowly gives way to pride, power, and violence.
At first, we understand Walter. But eventually, we have to confront the possibility that understanding him does not mean we should continue rooting for him.

While there is an exciting rush in rooting for an anti-hero, it also comes with moral discomfort. There comes a point when sympathy begins to resemble complicity–we recognize that Walter has begun crossing lines, yet because we’ve seen his beginning, a part of us remain invested in seeing how far his choices would take him.

Rafe Cameron from ‘Outer Banks’ is another similarly complicated character–violent, unpredictable, and responsible for some truly destructive decisions. There is a divide among fans of the Netflix series as to whether he deserved a good ending, but many continue to point to his familial struggles and desperate need for approval as reasons to believe he is capable of redemption.

Rafe is especially interesting because he makes the very question of character redemption harder to answer. It’s easy to sympathize with characters whose mistakes carry little consequences, but that same sympathy becomes far more difficult when their actions have caused genuine harm to others.

Jonas Pate, creator of ‘Outer Banks,’ ultimately decided to give Rafe’s character another chance at life and atonement. By the series finale, Rafe turned away from his destructive past and reconciled with his sister Sarah before beginning a new life with his girlfriend Sofia, suggesting that redemption remains possible even after a significant amount of harmful choices.
And perhaps that is what makes characters like these so compelling.
Why we root for the morally gray
Understanding a character is not the same as excusing them.

We can think a character is terrible and still find their story fascinating. We can condemn their actions while hoping they succeed. We can even love watching a character without wanting anything about them in our actual lives.
Anti-heroes–and the morally gray characters who exist alongside them–let us explore the uncomfortable gray areas of morality without having to live with the consequences ourselves.
They challenge our ideas of who deserves sympathy and redemption, and whether being a good person is really as simple as doing the right thing.

Maybe we don’t root for anti-heroes because we think they are like us. Maybe we root for them because, somewhere between the red flags and bad decisions, they give us a story complicated enough to care about.

articles.title: Magyar vs. Moscow: Hungary's new tough stance toward Russia
articles.summary: Hungarian PM Peter Magyar has abruptly ended the era of his predecessor's warm relations with Russia: Budapest has expelled 10 Russian diplomats from the country. Moscow is considering halting gas…

image.caption: The close and friendly ties between Hungary and Russia ended when Peter Magyar became prime minister earlier this yearImage: Attila Kisbenedek/AFP

blocks.text: While Viktor Orban was in power, no other EU member state was as pro-Russian as Hungary. Indeed, the former prime minister's apparent eagerness to be of service to the Russian president earned him the nickname "Putin's pinscher" or "Kremlin agent."
For years, Hungary was seen as a security risk both in the EU and NATO. Russian spies were able to operate in the country largely unhindered for a long time.
In February, it came to light that former Foreign Minister Peter Szijjarto had passed on confidential information from EU meetings to his Russian counterpart, Sergey Lavrov.
All this came to an end in May, when the new government headed by Peter Magyar took office.
An unambiguous signal to Moscow
In a clear departure from the government line under Orban, Hungary's new prime minister has already heavily criticized Russia's war of aggression against Ukraine several times.
The government also recently declared Russia a threat to Hungary's national security.

This week, it took its biggest step yet against Russia, expelling 10 Russian diplomats for engaging in activities "that are unacceptable for diplomats under the Vienna Convention," as announced by Hungarian Foreign Minister Anita Orban (no relation to the former prime minister).

blocks.caption: Hungarian Foreign Minister Anita Orban announced this week that Hungary was expelling 10 Russian embassy staff for activities 'that are unacceptable for diplomats under the Vienna Convention'Image: Daniel Vogl/dpa/picture alliance

blocks.text: Although Orban did not provide any more details, the phrase is generally understood to mean that the diplomats in question were spies.

The minister went on to say that the decision "protects Hungary's security and sovereignty," adding, "It does not imply breaking off diplomatic relations with Russia. Hungary intends to continue the necessary dialogue, based on mutual respect and adherence to the rules."
Back to old alliances

The minister's brief announcement immediately generated a huge number of headlines and comments — hardly surprising given that this was not only evidence of the government's 180° turn on the country's policy toward Russia but also one of the toughest diplomatic sanctions targeting Moscow since the collapse of communism in 1989/1990.

Speaking to Hungarian news website Index, secret service expert Peter Tarjani said that this was "not a diplomatic conflict, but a serious secret service matter" and that with this decision, Hungary was simultaneously returning "to the mainstream of its allies' security policy."

Political scientist and leading Hungarian Russia expert Andras Racz told the Hungarian national news agency MTI that Hungary was the only EU and NATO member not to have made such an expulsion in recent years.
Racz said that such a step "should really have been taken four-and-a-half years ago," adding that "Hungary is now settling its old debt with its allies."
Reliance on Russian gas?
Under Viktor Orban, Hungary was in fact the only EU country never to unreservedly condemn Russia's all-out war against Ukraine.
Indeed, during the last two years of his rule, Orban even blamed Ukraine and the West for Russia's aggression.

blocks.caption: The Russian Embassy in BudapestImage: Aled Betts/cc-by/Wikimedia Commons

blocks.text: But long before that — even after he came to power back in 2010 — Viktor Orban took a markedly pro-Russian line, which he justified, among other things, with the claim that Hungary was more dependent on Russian energy supplies than almost any other country in the region.

His government's repeated assertion that Russian gas was cheaper has long been disproved. What's more, the expansion of the Paks nuclear power plant with Russian support will cost Hungary dearly for decades to come.
In the light of all this, Orban's close ties to Russia remain a mystery.
Absurd situations

For Hungary, this closeness to Russia often led to absurd situations in which the country's national security was put at risk. At the same time, Orban repeatedly told his critics that it was they who were a threat to Hungary's sovereignty.
For example, Russian secret service agents for years took part in military-style training exercises in the far-right scene right up until 2016.

Starting in 2012, Russian secret service operatives for years stole huge amounts of data from the Hungarian Foreign Ministry and other Hungarian authorities without the government ever publicly condemning it.

In 2019, Russia got permission to move the headquarters of the International Investment Bank (IIB) to Budapest. The IIB was known as the "spy bank" because its leadership was made up of individuals linked to or associated with Russia's FSB intelligence service. It was only after the US imposed sanctions on the bank in 2023 that it left Hungary again.

Investigative journalist Szabolcs Panyi has warned multiple times in recent years that Hungary had become a "logistical center and deployment zone for Russian secret services," thereby putting the whole region at risk.
Rejection of Orban's pro-Russian course
Orban's strictly pro-Russian course was laterally rejected by many Hungarians.

blocks.caption: Former Prime Minister Viktor Orban (left, pictured here with Russian President Vladimir Putin in 2025) maintained close ties with Russia while he was in powerImage: Alexander Nemenov/Pool/AFP

blocks.text: The decidedly pro-European and pro-Western orientation of Peter Magyar and his Tisza party had a considerable role to play in their election victory earlier this year. The EU flag was often seen and spontaneous cries of "Russians, go home" often heard at election rallies last spring.

Unlike Viktor Orban, Magyar and leading politicians in his Tisza party are convinced that Hungary's place is exclusively in Europe and that the country should only maintain pragmatic, low-level relations with Russia.
Nevertheless, many observers and experts are surprised at how radically the Magyar government has turned away from Russia.

Andras Telkes, the former deputy head of Hungary's foreign intelligence service (IH), wrote in the newspaper Nepszava that the expulsion of diplomats shows that the presence of Russian secret services in Hungary obviously runs "very deep" and that the country has a serious problem.
Telkes says that the expulsion of 10 diplomats will help rebuild trust in Hungary in the eyes of the secret services of its NATO allies.
At the same time, he emphasizes the scale of the move: "Expelling two or three people would have been a sign. Expelling 10 people already means war."
Telkes went on to say that the move creates a serious security problem for Hungary.
Will Moscow turn off the taps?

The spokeswoman for the Russian Foreign Ministry condemned the expulsion of Russian diplomats in unusually strong terms: She spoke of a "Russophobe lobby in Budapest" and announced a "hard and painful" response.
Russian lawmaker Andrey Kolesnik, a member of the State Duma's Defense Committee, said that halting gas supplies to Hungary would have to be considered.

Hungary's Foreign Minister Anita Orban knows more about such Russian threats than anyone else in the new Hungarian government: She wrote her doctoral thesis in 2007 on Russia's energy policy in Central Europe. A year later, she published a book entitled "Power, Energy, and the New Russian Imperialism."
This article was originally published in German.

articles.title: Philippines ferry fire: Search continues for dozens missing
articles.summary: Firefighters searching for survivors combed through the smoking remains of a ferry off the coast of Coron island in the Philippines. Five people died and over 40 have been rescued

image.caption: The fire pm the MV June Aster continued to smolder Friday morning Image: Philippine Coast Guard/REUTERS

blocks.text: Philippine firefighters on Friday managed to enter a smoldering ferry in a search for dozens of people still unaccounted for after the vessel caught fire on Wednesday evening, with rescue work complicated by heavy smoke and extreme heat.
Firefighters have reported that five people have died, 43 people have been rescued, and more than 80 are missing.

The ferry "MV June Aster" had originated in Manila, and was nearing its destination, the tourist hotspot of Coron in the western Philippine province of Palawan, when it caught fire just off the coast.
The Philippine Coast Guard updated the number of missing people from 86 to 84 after confirming that two people originally listed on the manifest had not been on board.

blocks.caption: The Philippine Coast Guard said the ship caught fire in 'seconds' Image: Philippine Coast Guard/AP Photo/picture alliance

blocks.text: Ferry fire spread 'in seconds'
Philippine Coast Guards spokeswoman Noemie Cayabyab told a radio interview Friday that the fire broke out in "seconds."
"From the time that they heard the loud explosion, the appearance of smoke, and then fire. It spread very quickly," she said, citing survivor accounts.
Cayabyab said some of those who made it off the ship did not have time to put on life jackets.

blocks.caption: Some passengers jumped into the water and were rescued by nearby fishermenImage: Philippine Coast Guard/AFP

blocks.text: The Coast Guard has deployed several vessels and divers to the incident, while army rescue boats, fishermen and private resort owners have also provided assistance in the search.
Investigation ongoing
The fire began in the cargo hold, and may have moved even more rapidly due to strong winds, Cayabyab added later.
Although the exact cause of the accident has yet to be officially determined, survivors reported hearing explosions inside the ship.
They later said that a small fire quickly escalated and engulfed the vessel.

blocks.caption: The Coast Guard released this image of the ferry burning Wednesday night Image: Philippine Coast Guard/AFP

blocks.text: Some passengers jumped into the sea, where they remained afloat until they were rescued. The vessel caught fire some 7 kilometers (4.5 miles) off the village of Turda.
The ferry was carrying electric cars, motorcycles, cargo, and heavy-duty equipment, as well as provisions for the crew and passengers.
Ferries are one of the most widely used forms of transport in the Philippines, an archipelago made up of 7,600 islands.
The country has a history of maritime accidents, some of which are caused by overcrowding, adverse sailing conditions, and lax safety standards.

articles.title: Pleased.com sets up BGC headquarters
articles.summary: Customer service software firm Pleased.com has opened its headquarters in Bonifacio Global City (BGC), investing in Filipino tech talent as it plans to hire more than 100 workers over the next year.…

blocks.text: Customer service software firm Pleased.com has opened its headquarters in Bonifacio Global City (BGC), investing in Filipino tech talent as it plans to hire more than 100 workers over the next year.
The company, founded about four years ago in Europe, formally opened its Philippine office at the Three/NEO Building in BGC this week. It had previously operated remotely from Europe.
Pleased.com plans to hire between 100 and 110 employees in the Philippines over the next 12 months, with most positions intended for technology and product roles.
The company has already hired its administrative staff and around 10 engineers locally. It is targeting 50 engineers by the end of the year.
“We want to go where the best talent and the best infrastructure is,” founder and CEO Jonathan Sterling said when asked why the company chose Taguig over lower-cost locations.
“I really feel like the best talent and the best infrastructure is specifically in BGC,” Sterling added.
Pleased.com provides live chat, email ticketing and voice support software to businesses.
Its platform currently handles six million to seven million customer contacts annually for enterprise clients, including Lithuanian credit institution Unlokk and African digital bank Tenn.io.
Sterling shared that artificial intelligence (AI) resolves about 75 percent of client contacts from start to finish, while it automatically routes frustrated customers to human agents.
Despite its use of the technology, Sterling stressed that Pleased.com considers itself a customer service software provider rather than an AI company.

The Philippine expansion will also support the company’s push into the small and mid-sized business market, primarily in the United States. Pleased.com wants to make its customer service platform easier for smaller companies to deploy without extensive technical work.
Sterling said the company was particularly looking for engineers and workers with bachelor’s and master’s degrees in science, technology, engineering and mathematics fields.
Pleased.com completed the BGC office within three months after leasing the initially bare unit.

Taguig Mayor Lani Cayetano, who attended the office opening, said the investment could help connect Filipino talent with global opportunities. Philippine Economic Zone Authority representative Ligaya Jennifer Escolano and executives of Neo Group were also present. /pai

articles.title: Anthropic blocks possible attempt to use AI to make biological weapons
articles.summary: The revelations in Anthropic's threat intelligence report come after a former top researcher at the company warned of the risks of AI to humanity.

blocks.text: Anthropic says it has identified and disrupted attempts to use its AI model for "malicious activity" which could support the development of biological weapons.

The findings, made in the firm's recent threat intelligence report, is the latest in a growing series of warnings from AI researchers and industry insiders about the technology's potential risks to humanity.
The warnings have prompted calls to action, with US Senator Bernie Sanders demanding a pause on advanced AI development and a ban on artificial superintelligence.
President Donald Trump has so far rejected such fears, saying on Thursday he was concerned "if we don't win AI, we're going to be put in a very bad position".
The company published its latest threat intelligence report, external on Thursday. Other AI firms publish similar reports.

This includes Google, which wrote on Tuesday, external a person had attempted to use its AI tool Gemini to obtain a "complete, step-by-step technical guide for synthesizing weaponised biological agents".
Anthropic's AI model Claude was also used by actors linked to a Russia-based cyber espionage campaign and by an Iranian propaganda institution, according to Anthropic's report.
The cases of concern detected over the past eight months ranged from fake dating apps and hotel Wifi scams, to surveillance built to identify dissidents.
Anthropic has also accused Chinese AI firms of trying to replicate Claude's capabilities.
The lengthy report lists cases in which suspected state-sponsored groups, criminals, spyware vendors, state propaganda institutions and politically motivated individuals misused its technology.
"Malicious use" of its Claude Haiku, Sonnet, and Opus models was disrupted between December 2025 and August 2026, it said.

None of the misuse cases involved Claude Fable or the powerful Mythos-class models, with the exception of one instance of distillation - the process for training smaller AI models using larger, more expensive models.

As well as detecting the use of its models for cyber and influence operations, surveillance, scams and fraud and weapon development, Anthropic said it had blocked scientists who used its AI in ways that could support biological weapons development.
The report highlighted "five case studies of actors using our models in ways that could support biological weapons development".
Biological misuse, it said, is "one of the most serious risks of frontier AI model". Without the correct safeguards, such capabilities "could have catastrophic consequences", Anthropic said.
"The same information that can be used to develop a biological weapon could also be used to develop, for example, a vaccine or a cure for a disease," Anthropic said.
Jacob Klein, the head of threat intelligence at Anthropic, told the New York Times, external it was "an incredibly nuanced situation".
"You are not seeing someone in a comic book kind of way say, 'Hey, I want to build a biological weapon to kill everybody,'" he said.

The report also noted six cases where Claude was used "to develop software for conventional weapons, including firearms, missiles, armed drones, bombs, and other munitions, as well as the targeting and control systems that operate them".
The report indicated that cybercriminals and state-backed hackers have increasingly used its technology to assist their operations.
Hacking group ShinyHunters, as well as China-based labs, were among those named in the report.

The report also said that a hacking group whose work is consistent with the Russia-based Midnight Blizzard allegedly used AI to build a system that automatically detected when its malware was flagged by security defences and rewrote code until it evaded detection.
The California-based company said it had incorporated its findings into its processes "to better prevent, detect, and disrupt these activities in the future".
Anthropic said it had shared intelligence with authorities and industry partners where appropriate.

The report - the company's first this year - comes after a top safety researcher at Anthropic warned AI is advancing so quickly he believes there is a greater than 10% chance it "could kill all humans" within the next decade.
In an article published on 6 September, OpenAI chief scientist Jakub Pachocki called for the industry to implement "voluntary slowdowns" until safeguards are set.

"I am concerned no one is prepared for the consequences of a continued rapid rise in machine intelligence," Pachocki said, adding that OpenAI, which makes ChatGPT, will continue its work on building safeguards, though broader interventions are required.

The warning prompted an open letter to UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham calling for a new multinational treaty for the safe development of AI and a call for governments to collaborate about what a treaty based on the development of superintelligence should look like.
In the US, Democratic lawmaker Bernie Sanders has introduced legislation to ban AI superintelligence and temporarily pause advanced AI development.
"When scientists tell you there is a chance, a chance that it could have a cataclysmic impact on humanity, you've got be a moron not to say, slow it down," he said on Thursday on BBC's Newsnight.
With additional reporting from Osmond Chia.
